mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive monthly observations
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) following three consecutive monthly FEDFUNDS increases in at least 70% of historical tightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY falls below -0.5%, or the effect reverses in more than 50% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% combined with a concurrent drop in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals an overheating labor market followed by a sudden correction, which historically precedes negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of such joint trigger events.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 70% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below its 12-month average, combined with a concurrent drop in real personal savings (RSAFS), signals a housing demand shock that reduces household wealth and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 12-month MA AND RSAFS < 12-month MA for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of such joint trigger events.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period where the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is below its 12-month moving average while FEDFUNDS remains near zero signals a low-inflation, low-rate environment that boosts present value of cash flows and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 12-month MA AND FEDFUNDS <= 0.25% for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least 60% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for three consecutive months signals a deepening labor market slack, which reduces corporate earnings power and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 70% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive year-over-year growth in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 4% coinciding with a rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals robust demand expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth > 4% AND PAYEMS rises month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least 60% of such joint trigger events.
